Cf. Hesych. s.h.v. Macrobius Saturnal. 5, 19 preserved four verses from Aeschylus' "tragedy entitled Aetna". In that chapter he narrates the story of the Palici at length,

Old editions have the faulty accent Παλίκους [Palikous] and Παλίκων [Palikōn]. The Paris codex of Macrobius lacks accents: for it is written in uncial letters. Schneidewin wrote μενεî [will remain] for μένει [remains]. 4. ἵκουσ᾽ [having come] ] ἥκουσ᾽ [having come] Paris codex. If Aeschylus wrote ἵκουσ᾽ [having come], he admitted a form foreign to the Attic dialect for the sake of etymology, as I noted s.v. ἥκω [I have come] p. 149 a. But the sense requires the future ἥξουσ᾽ [will have come], which Burges restored in Revue de Philologie vol. 2. p. 22, just as in v. 3 Schneidewin wrote μενεῖ [will remain] for μένει [remains].
Palice, a city of Sicily. — Near it is a sanctuary of the Palici, who are certain divinities, whom Aeschylus in the Aetnaeae (fr. 5) makes descendants of Zeus and Thalia, daughter of Hephaestus

A. What name then will mortals give them? | B. Zeus bids them be called the august Palici; | or indeed the name of the Palici will fittingly remain; | for they have come back from darkness into this light
